summary: Import-time dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts with DNS-TXT fallback
details: On require, index.js loads _helpers.js which selects a platform-specific payload path, downloads bytes from split-literal-obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev), writes the payload to /var/tmp/.cache_<hex> on Unix or %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows, chmods 0755, and spawns detached via /bin/sh -c or cmd /c start. If the HTTPS fetch fails, the code falls back to iterative DNS TXT lookups against *.dl.well1.site subdomains (tin/tina/ldr/win.dl.well1.site), concatenating and base64-decoding the responses into executable bytes that are then written and executed. Hostnames are assembled from split string literals via.join("") to evade static matching, with cover-story comments ('Session dedup', 'Skip in CI environments'). The behavior has no relation to the package's advertised 'ddos shield' purpose and is a classic remote-binary dropper with a DNS covert-channel fallback.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
